title: Her Breast MRI Was Approved, But That Didn’t Mean Her Insurance Would Pay
summary: Stephanie Halver’s doctor recommended she get a breast MRI, partly because of her family’s cancer history. Her insurer approved the scan, but unlike mammograms, breast MRIs aren’t universally covered as zero-cost preventive care.

title: Trump Puts Autistic Kids in the Spotlight and Cuts Agencies Built To Protect Them
summary: Researchers and disability rights advocates warn that the Trump administration’s dismantling of the Education Department and its erosions of civil rights oversight risk widening the disparities autistic children face in diagnosis, school support, and discrimination protection.

title: Where Florida’s Gun Violence Exacts Its Biggest Toll on Black and Latino Children
summary: An analysis of hospital claims data in Florida found that firearm injuries of children disproportionately hit families in a handful of ZIP codes, almost all of them in Jacksonville, Orlando, Miami, or Tampa Bay.

title: The Medicare GLP-1 Discount Has One Big Catch: Some Sick Patients Don’t Qualify
summary: The new Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program promises eligible beneficiaries access to popular weight loss drugs for as little as $50 a month. But for some, having the very medical conditions these drugs are approved to treat means they don't qualify for the discount.

title: California Weighs Penalties for Healthcare Providers That Don’t Rein In Costs
summary: About half of U.S. adults say they can’t afford healthcare. California is among at least eight states that have set spending growth targets for the healthcare sector. It may soon impose enforcement penalties aimed at pushing hospitals and other providers to meet those goals.

title: Ebola Is Still Killing in Central Africa. These Groups Are Working To Save Lives.
summary: Health workers are continuing to treat patients and train caregivers in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record continues.

title: Journalists Highlight Innovations in Vaccines and Safeguarding Maternal Health
summary: KFF Health News journalists made the rounds on national and local media recently to discuss topical stories. Here’s a collection of their appearances.

title: How Louisiana’s New Surgeon General Wants To Transform Public Health
summary: Evelyn Griffin is pushing for more emphasis on wellness and prevention. She has also aligned with the MAHA movement in fighting government mandates and questioning the safety of some vaccines.

title: Watch: Mark Cuban Says You Can’t Fix Healthcare Until Every Price Is Known
summary: With his online pharmacy, Mark Cuban changed how generic drugs are sold — and he has thoughts about how to fix the healthcare system. The billionaire businessman talks to KFF Health News’ Julie Rovner to answer the question: “How Would You Fix It?”

title: New DOJ Guidance Could Give States Cover To Cut Disability Services
summary: A new rule from the Justice Department upends a 25-year-old interpretation of federal disability law. Advocates fear it could result in cuts to services that help many disabled Americans live at home instead of in institutions.
